metadata.primary_source_paper: Raup, D. M. (1966). Geometric Analysis of Shell Coiling: General Problems. Journal of Paleontology, 40(5), 1178-1190.
metadata.original_introduction: Raup, D. M. (1962). Computer as Aid in Describing Form in Gastropod Shells. Science, 138(3537), 150-152.
metadata.ammonoid_application: Raup, D. M. (1967). Geometric Analysis of Shell Coiling: Coiling in Ammonoids. Journal of Paleontology, 41(1), 43-65.
metadata.note: The three-parameter model (W, D, T) was first introduced in Raup (1962). The 1966 paper provides the detailed mathematical formulation. The 1967 paper applies the model to ammonoids.
metadata.revision_2026_10_17: Model definitions corrected and parameter sets replaced after the MorphoEval audit of 2026-10-13. The earlier 'definition' strings and the per-shell 'source' page/figure attributions were produced by an AI assistant without access to the paper and could not be verified; the T definition ('vertical rise per radian') was wrong and led to a script in which T had no effect. Definitions below follow Raup & Michelson 1965 / Raup 1966 as restated by Noshita 2014 (J Theor Biol 363:93-104) and Okabe & Yoshimura 2017 (Sci Rep 7:42445): D is the inner/outer margin ratio of the generating curve and T the axial translation of its centre per unit of radial movement. The six parameter sets are illustrative points in the morphospace chosen so that each descriptive name is geometrically true; they are NOT values Raup measured for the taxa named with 'cf.'. The 'typical_range' values are likewise indicative, not quoted from the paper.

W.name: Whorl Expansion Rate
W.definition: Whorl expansion rate: every linear dimension of the generating curve, and its distance from the axis, is multiplied by W per revolution (a(theta) = a0 * W^(theta/2pi)).

source.note: Raup 1966; definition restated from Noshita 2014 / Okabe & Yoshimura 2017 (paper not consulted directly)

W.effect: Higher W = wider, more rapidly expanding shells

D.name: Distance from Coiling Axis
D.definition: Relative distance of the generating curve from the coiling axis: the distance of its inner margin from the axis divided by that of its outer margin, D = (r_c - a)/(r_c + a). D = 0: the inner margin touches the axis (involute, no umbilicus); larger D: open umbilicus.

source.note: Raup 1966; definition restated from Noshita 2014 / Okabe & Yoshimura 2017 (paper not consulted directly)

D.effect: D=0 = inner margin on the axis (no umbilicus); higher D = more open, evolute forms

T.name: Translation Rate
T.definition: Translation rate: the movement of the generating curve's centre along the coiling axis per unit of its movement away from the axis, T = dz_c/dr_c (so z_c = T * r_c and the spire scales with the whorls). T = 0 is planispiral.

source.note: Raup 1966; definition restated from Noshita 2014 / Okabe & Yoshimura 2017 (paper not consulted directly)

T.effect: T=0 = planispiral (flat), higher T = elongated, turreted forms

S.name: Shape of Generating Curve
S.definition: Shape of the generating curve, here the ratio of its radial to its axial semi-axis (repository convention; S = 1 circular).

source.note: Raup 1966 defines S as the generating curve's shape; the direction of the ratio used here is the repository's convention

S.effect: S=1 = circular, S>1 = wider than tall, S<1 = taller than wide

empirical_shells.name: Planispiral
empirical_shells.note: involute planispiral: T = 0, inner margin on the axis

empirical_shells.name: Turreted
empirical_shells.note: slow expansion, high translation: a tall narrow spire of many whorls

empirical_shells.name: Conical
empirical_shells.note: fast expansion with moderate translation: a cone with a short spire and a large last whorl

empirical_shells.name: Globose
empirical_shells.note: fast expansion, low translation: a rounded shell with a low spire

mathematical_formulation.generating_curve_semi_axis: a(theta) = a0 * W^(theta / 2pi)   (radial); b = a / S (axial)
mathematical_formulation.centre_distance_from_axis: r_c(theta) = a(theta) * (1 + D) / (1 - D)   so that (r_c - a)/(r_c + a) = D
mathematical_formulation.centre_position_along_axis: z_c(theta) = T * r_c(theta)   so that dz_c/dr_c = T
mathematical_formulation.surface: X = (r_c + a cos phi) cos theta;  Y = (r_c + a cos phi) sin theta;  Z = z_c + b sin phi   (generating curve in the radial-axial plane)
mathematical_formulation.source: Raup & Michelson 1965, Raup 1966, as restated by Noshita 2014 and Okabe & Yoshimura 2017 (T = x0/y0, D = (y0-1)/(y0+1) in their unit-circle coordinates)

empirical_shells_provenance: Illustrative points in Raup's morphospace chosen 2026-10-17 so that each descriptive name is geometrically true (see note per entry); 'common_name' is the kind of shell the form resembles ('cf.'), not a measured specimen. The 2025-01-05 values (Planispiral 2.0/0.05/0.1, Turreted 2.5/0.15/0.8, Disc-like 3.5/0.3/0.2, Conical 2.2/0.1/0.5, High-spired 1.8/0.12/1.2, Wide 3.0/0.25/0.3) carried page/figure attributions to Raup 1966 that could not be verified and rendered, even with the corrected model, as low-spired forms that did not match their names.
